statement: SemiAnalysis measures Vera Rubin NVL72 at between 1.4x and 3x the throughput per total cost of ownership of the latest GB300 TRTLLM configuration at a realistic 80 TPS P90 serving point, and roughly 67x on an apples-to-apples dense comparison at 170 TPS.
why: Cost per token delivered is the buying test for inference fleets; a next-generation part that lifts throughput per dollar pulls forward orders and shortens the useful economic life of installed Blackwell capacity.

impact.mechanism: Better throughput per TCO lowers the cost of serving agentic inference, raising the return on buying Rubin and increasing total accelerator demand while pressuring the resale economics of prior-generation racks.

evidence.excerpt: between 1.4x and 3x the throughput per TCO

confidence.basis: Single secondary analyst publication using its own ownership-cost assumptions; no vendor filing corroborates the figures, and the headline 67x applies only to a narrow 170 TPS dense comparison.

dispersion: 1.4x-3x at 80 TPS P90 under ownership TCO, versus approximately 67x at 170 TPS dense; 10x more tokens per USD than B300 at 80 TPS P90.
entity: NVIDIA / CoreWeave (Rubin NVL72 vs GB300 performance-per-cost)
